text:
Priya: Quick sync - eu-west GPU pool (eu-west-1-gpu-a) hit sustained ~94-96% for ~40m yesterday. Interactive chat p95 jumped from ~170ms -> ~420ms, some users saw >3s queue waits. Current setup is global FIFO with simple per-route rate limits. Thinking we need a better backpressure strategy - FIFO isn't cutting it under mixed short/long workloads. Thoughts?

Liam: Can you drop the breakdown? single pool or cross-region? :thinking_face:

Priya: Single pool. Traffic mix: interactive chat = ~68% of requests (short token counts), long-running batch rerank jobs = ~18% of requests but very high token/compute. Batch saturates GPU time despite lower request count. Cost: batch cheaper per token but kills tail latency.

Sam: We've prototyped per-route weighted admission before. Upstream per-route queues, global admission controller issues execution tickets based on pool capacity. Uses per-route weights so interactive gets more tickets but not absolute priority. Avoids hard starvation.

Jules: Another pattern is priority queues with aging: high priority for interactive/enterprise, low for batch/offline, then bump priority after X ms so long-waiters eventually promote. Keeps fairness while favoring interactive.

Liam: Hybrid idea: per-route queues + admission token bucket. tokens_per_sec = floor(gpu_cores * 0.85 / avg_cost). Autoscaler can nudge tokens up if util < 70% for 5m. This ties rate limits to actual capacity.

Sam: Heres a config we used internally (simplified):

```yaml
queue_strategy: per_route_weighted
routes:
  interactive:
    weight: 4
  batch:
    weight: 1
admission:
  token_bucket_size: 120
  refill_qps: 220
```

Jules: Tradeoffs: per-route queues increase control but can fragment packing - small interactive tasks leave holes that batch can't use efficiently. Priority queues simpler but risk starving batch under sustained load. Aging helps.

Priya: What about preemption? If a long batch runs >time_budget, preempt and requeue. But that loses KV cache / context which harms interactive quality if we preempt interactive tasks. Maybe only preempt cheap stateless batch reranks.

Liam: Agreed. Preempt only stateless batch or rerank jobs. For stateful long jobs, prefer chunking into smaller units.

Sam: Proposal for a controlled experiment:
- Enable priority-with-aging on eu-west pool as a canary handling ~10% of traffic for 48h.
- Export metrics: p95/p99 per-route, queue_wait_histogram, gpu_util, queued_count_by_route, aborts/retries.
- Success criteria: interactive p95 improves >=20% and batch throughput drop <=10% and no >3% error increase.

Jules: Config snippet for priority+aging canary:

```yaml
queue_strategy: priority_with_aging
priorities:
  high: [interactive, enterprise]
  med: [api, scheduled]
  low: [batch, offline]
aging_ms: 300000  # 5min to promote
fifo_within_priority: true
canary: { region: eu-west-1-gpu-a, traffic_pct: 10 }
```

Priya: Action items:
- Jules: add feature flag + rollout pipeline for eu-west canary (assign to you)
- Sam: add admission-controller metrics and Grafana panels (tokens_available, queued_by_route, avg_wait_ms, promotions)
- Liam: expose tokens_per_second heuristic and autoscaler hook to auto-increase tokens if util < 70% for 5m
- Priya: build dashboard and define alert SLOs (interactive p95, queue_depth, stalled_jobs)

Jules: I'll open a PR today. Thinking canary rollout schedule: 5% -> 30m, 25% -> 2h, then 10% stable for 48h. Will include smoke tests.

Sam: I'll also add a synthetic load test mix that includes 90% short requests and 10% long tails so we can validate packing and fragmentation effects.

Liam: One more safety knob: fallback routing to a smaller / quantized model for interactive requests when pool is near-saturation. Lower quality but keeps latency low. Use that as a mitigation path instead of full preemption.

Priya: Good point. Add fallback model route in rollback plan and estimate cost savings.

Jules: PR opened -> #3456 with config and tests. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: started canary rollout to eu-west (5%) - rollout id rlt-2026-03-12-091

Priya: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the 6h check and review metrics. :calendar:
